item.title: NASA Receives 16th Consecutive ‘Clean’ Financial Audit Opinion
item.description: For the 16th consecutive year, NASA has received an unmodified, or “clean,” opinion from an external auditor on its fiscal year 2026 financial statements. The rating is the best possible audit opinion, certifying that NASA’s financial statements conform with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles for federal agencies

item.title: Forget the Lineage: Forward-Secure, Lineage-Complete Cryptographic Erasure for LLM-Agent Memory
item.description: Large language model (LLM) agents keep a long-term memory that the model itself writes: summaries, extracted facts and embeddings derived from what users said. Deleting a message is therefore not enough: its derivatives, storage residue and backups survive.

item.title: They Will See Johnny's Message: A Measurement Study of Post-Quantum Cryptography Across Email Delivery Paths
item.description: Harvest-now, decrypt-later (HNDL) attacks make the transition to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) urgent for email. This paper presents a systematic measurement that jointly examines PQC deployment across email service stages, negotiation by communicating peers, and usable message encryption.

item.title: Grounding Object-to-Object Hazard Reasoning into 3D Risk Fields for Task-Conditioned Safety
item.description: Safety in robotics does not solely depend on geometric constraints, but also on semantics: the given task, environment properties, and interactions between objects in the scene. We present a framework based on vision-language models (VLMs) to infer task- and scene-dependent safety constraints for robot manipulation.

item.title: Aligning AI Teams
item.description: Previous work has shown that alignment training on individual LLM agents can fail to transfer to multi-agent settings. We investigate the underlying mechanisms for this failure, and explore interventions to preserve alignment transfer to multi-agent LLM teams.

item.title: Heuristic Lookahead Distillation Protocol Search
item.description: Bipartite qubit entanglement distillation is the process of converting noisy ebits into pure ebits using only local operations and classical communication. This is a core operation for quantum repeaters, enabling such crucial tasks as long-distance quantum communication and distributed quantum computing.
